source: NCERT Class VII, Our Environment, Geography Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. Interior of the Earth — Three Layers
points: **Crust** — the **outermost, thinnest** layer; the solid land we live on. Continental crust is mainly **silica + alumina (SIAL)**; oceanic crust mainly **silica + magnesium (SIMA)**.
Crust thickness: about **35 km under continents**, only about **5 km under oceans**.
**Mantle** — the middle layer, extending to about **2900 km** deep.
**Core** — the **innermost** layer; mainly **nickel and iron (NIFE)**; the **hottest**; the inner core is solid, the outer core liquid.

sections.heading: 2. Rocks
points: **Rock** = any natural mass of **minerals**; a single natural substance = a **mineral**.

sub: **Igneous** — formed when **molten magma/lava cools and solidifies** (e.g. basalt, granite); called 'primary' rocks. Intrusive (granite) vs extrusive (basalt).
**Sedimentary** — formed when **sediments** are compressed in **layers** (e.g. sandstone); may contain **fossils**.
**Metamorphic** — formed when igneous/sedimentary rocks change under **heat and pressure** (e.g. clay → slate, limestone → marble, coal → diamond).

sections.heading: 3. The Rock Cycle
points: Rocks change from one type to another over time — the **rock cycle**.
**Molten magma cools → igneous**; igneous **weathers/erodes → sediments → sedimentary**; heat & pressure change either → **metamorphic**; deep heat melts rock back to **magma**.
Rocks are used as **minerals, fuels, building materials**, tools; they are a key **resource**.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Earth's layers: Crust (thinnest) → Mantle → Core (hottest, NiFe).
Continental crust = SIAL (silica+alumina); oceanic = SIMA (silica+magnesium); core = NIFE.
Igneous = cooled magma/lava (primary); sedimentary = compressed layers (fossils); metamorphic = heat & pressure.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Crust** is the thinnest layer; the **core** is the innermost and hottest (nickel + iron).
**Igneous** rocks are 'primary' — formed from cooled magma/lava.
**Fossils** are found in **sedimentary** rocks (formed in layers).
**Marble** is a **metamorphic** rock (from limestone); **granite** is igneous.
